own_solution.law: Wien displacement law lambda_max T = const, calibrated by the first star; E = hc/lambda
assumptions: maximum per unit wavelength in both cases

notes: lambda_2 = 500 nm * 5800/2900 = 1000 nm, E = 1240/1000 = 1.24 eV. With the 950 K rise before recording, T = 3850 K, lambda = 753.25 nm, E = 1.24*3850/2900 = 1.6462 eV. A rise after the spectrum was recorded does not affect the recorded peak; the third star has no path to the target. TEFF6/T2C66 and T099E/TFD41 appear to be numbered/numeral-free versions of the same sentence; the 950 K variants all state the same number and unit. The 2900 K in the problem is read as the quiescent temperature, which an outburst then raises; this is coherent but slightly artificial.
